Note (goes to the report at once):
The first category, %1, starts at row %2 - nothing above
%1 is not first: starts at row %2, others are higher
All %1 layout places hold their own things
Floor grid: drawing %1 ms a frame, building %2 ms a frame on average (last build %3 ms)
The hammer is far from the tools (cell %1)
The hammer is next to the tools (cell %1)
Layout places %1, empty %2, no other things on them
No test pack: press Prepare in point 1.
No hammer added yet (or it is not in the pack)
The pack has no layout: right click the header > Save layout.
No second screwdriver yet (or the first is not in the pack)
The line is not in the file as read: exit to the menu and load again
The screwdriver is far from the first one (cell %1)
The screwdriver is by the first one (cell %1)
Blocks out of order or something did not fit: %1
Blocks follow the order of categories (first row): %1
Open settings - the Order tab. Take a category's row with the mouse and drag it up or down. Then try the arrows left of the rows.
While a row is dragged the others make room where it would go; let go, it stays there. The arrows move it one row; the first has no up arrow, the last no down arrow.
Open settings - the Order tab opens. Move Food and water to the top with Up, close the window and sort the pack.
Food is now the first block, top left. The rule and New things on that tab work at once too.
Pick a bandage up with the mouse, swing it fast back and forth, then stop the mouse sharply. Do the same with an axe and a full pack (Prepare in point 1 if there is none).
A light thing barely lags behind the cursor. A heavy one trails it and sways a little after the stop - the heavier, the more. It is put where the cursor is, not where the lagging picture is.
Drop 300 things - a pile appears around you. Pick the Floor in Surroundings, move the mouse, sort, watch the FPS. Then Check and Remove the pile.

FPS with the floor open nearly as without the inventory. Check shows how many ms a frame the floor's grid took since the last press: press once, wait five seconds with the floor on screen, press again. Under 1 ms is good.
Search for something lying in several places (bandage), open the Found window. Draw a frame from an empty place over a few things, Ctrl+click one in or out, then Shift+click a picked one or drag it.
Picked tiles are lighter in a white frame; the same things are picked in the grids too. Shift and dragging move everything picked at once. A click on an empty place drops the pick.
Faded copies in the next body (Sharp)

Press "Two bodies": two bodies appear on one square next to you, one with an axe, a crowbar, a sledgehammer and a hammer, the other with apples and a pencil. Open the inventory, pick the body with the tools in Surroundings, Shift+click the tools one by one (or Take all) and, while they are still moving, pick the other body in the list.

THE BUG (now): the other body's grid shows faded copies of the tools being moved. AFTER THE FIX: the faded copies stay only in the body the tools are leaving. The check says whether the two bodies share a grid key (the cause).
On a pack with a layout and empty places press the eye by the Sort button. Then once more.
The eye closes (the lids meet in a line with lashes), the silhouettes fade; pressed again it opens and they come back. The eye is only where there is a layout, and it works for every bag at once.

Press "Pot of water": a pot of tainted water appears in your pockets. Put it on a lit stove (or in an oven) and watch its tile in the stove's grid while it heats. Then take it off and let it cool. Also look at a bottle of water from a working fridge.

The pot's tile turns red as it heats, brighter the hotter - as the row in the game's own inventory. Taken off, it fades back. A cold thing from a fridge is tinted blue. Food keeps its own cooking colours.

Stand by a car, open its trunk (Surroundings shows it). Press "Generator": a generator appears in your hands. Drag it from a hand slot into the trunk's grid (also try dropping it on the trunk's row in the list).
The generator goes into the trunk after the progress bar, as the move shows. It does NOT fall to the ground. Taken out of the hands by double click it still falls to the ground, as in the game.
Move the mouse slowly over the tiles of a grid, rest on one.
The tile under the mouse rises a couple of pixels with a small hop, a shadow under it; the tile above doesn't cover it. Mouse gone - it settles back. With animations off nothing moves.
On the character screen page through the clothing layers backwards (the left arrow): reach the first and press once more.
From the first layer it goes to the last, no errors, no empty layer.
In the test pack put the screwdriver in a corner (bottom left), move the other tools away and save the layout. Take the screwdriver out of the pack, then Add a hammer.
The hammer lands on the screwdriver's place (it has no place of its own in the layout, the tool's place is empty). A second hammer - as near the tools' places as there is room. Sort keeps it so.
Shift+click each of the three things in the pockets (the pack must be the active container - click its header).
Each thing lands exactly on its silhouette; no silhouettes left.
Move a few things in the pack by hand. Right click the header > Save layout. Then press Take 3 things out here.
Three things went to the pockets; their places in the pack show pale silhouettes with their icons. The header menu now has Forget layout.
Take 3 things out, sort the pack, change the rule and sort again. Then Put them back, no place - they come in as picked-up things do.
With any rule the layout's things stay on their places, the rest packs around, nothing else sits on the silhouettes. The returned things land on their silhouettes.
A second one of a kind goes by the first
Press Prepare, then right click the pack's header > Forget layout. Move the screwdriver to any corner. Then One more screwdriver: the second goes into the pack without a place picked.
The new screwdriver lies right by the first one, wherever it is, not in the first cell of the tools.
New thing next to its category
Right click the header > Forget layout, sort. Then Add a hammer here: it goes into the pack without a place picked.
The hammer lands next to the tools, not in the first free cell.
Pick a cupboard in Surroundings and right click its header. Then open a bag's window (double click a bag) and right click its header. Try Sort and Save layout there.
The menu with Sort, the rule and the layout is everywhere; a cupboard's layout stays after you leave and come back. The floor and corpses keep no layout - that is right.
Add the line puts 'Base.Hammer = category mat' into Zomboid/Lua/knox_overrides.txt. Exit to the main menu, load the save, open the bench again and press Check. Remove the line at the end.
Hammers have the materials background and sort into the materials block. After Remove the line and a reload - tools again.
Bandages puts a stack of 3 into the pockets and 2 on the floor. Click the pack's header (it becomes active), pick the Floor in Surroundings and Shift+click the bandages there.
The floor's bandages joined the stack in the pockets instead of a new tile in the pack. A full stack takes what fits, the rest goes apart. Check counts the bandage tiles on you.

Open settings - the Look tab, the Skin part with its Beta plate. Click through the skins, then move the Custom hue / saturation / brightness sliders. Look at the inventory, Surroundings, an item tooltip, bag windows, Found, the menu and the loading screen.

The skin changes at once, no reload: the main colour (frames, buttons, picks) and the windows' tone. Tiles keep their category colours. Text on coloured buttons stays readable. The choice is kept after exit. Note anything that stayed sand.
Right click the pack's header > Sort rule > Tight, By name, By weight in turn. Shuffle in between if you like.
The pack is repacked at once by the rule: tight - biggest first, no holes; by name - alphabetical; by weight - heaviest first. The current rule is marked (now). Set By category back at the end.
Press Prepare: a test ALICE pack with a mess of ~30 things goes on your back (if the back is taken, it opens in a window). Then press the Sort button (three bars) on its header.
Things lie in blocks by category in the settings' order, the same things side by side, the two bandage stacks and two nail stacks merged. Shuffle makes a mess again.
Bandages, if not done yet. Rest the mouse on a bandage on the floor, then pick it up with the mouse.
While the mouse is on it (or it is held), your bandage stack lights green - there is room. A full stack lights red. Things that don't stack (clothes, weapons) light nothing.

Press "Tent": the test ALICE pack goes on your back and a packed tent lies on the floor. Pick the tent up the way a player would: Shift+click, drag it into the pack, Take all. Then look for it: the pack's grid, the quick slots at the bottom of the screen, the hotbar with the inventory closed. Try to get it off.

Write down where the tent went and where you could see it. Expected: if it hangs on the "bottom of the backpack" slot, that slot shows in the quick slots row with the tent in it, and the tent can be dragged out or taken off with its menu.
Open a TV or a radio with several channels in the Knox window. Go to the first channel and press back, then again.
From the first channel it goes to the last, then back in order. No errors.
Split a stack / wear or equip
Lock / unlock the item under the cursor
Open a bag / use an item
Quick move to the other side
A bag with things in it won't go into another bag
Take this bag out of the other one first
Put the camp back as it was
Takes every keepsake away from the camp in the main menu. The things themselves stay in the heroes' bags.
Point at an occupation or a trait to read about it. A click on a trait takes it or gives it back.
Not enough points: give a positive trait back or take a negative one.

Which containers the Surroundings column lists. "Only the opened one": the one you opened by clicking it in the world or with Viewpoint's key, and the floor next to you. "Auto": that with Viewpoint's camera, everything around with the usual camera. In a car everything is always shown.

Where a thing goes when it is put in a bag without a place picked (Shift+click, Take all). By layout: to its place in the bag's saved layout, else next to things of its category. First free cell: as before.

What the Sort button on a bag's or container's header does. By category: each category in a block of its own, in the order below, the same things side by side, part stacks put together, food that spoils sooner first. Locked things stay where they are.

Click a plate, then make the gesture on this window: a click or a double click with Shift, Ctrl or Alt held, or a right click; for a key - press it, alone or with Shift, Ctrl, Alt. Esc cancels, Delete leaves the action unbound. A gesture taken from another action unbinds that one. Rotating can also go on the right or middle mouse button: while an item is held, it turns the item instead of opening a menu.
DEV: radios, TVs, bags and containers
LMB - turn   Shift+LMB - roll   RMB - move   wheel - zoom   2xLMB - reset

Knox Inventory needs ZombieBuddy, but its Java part did not load.

The game's own inventory is used for now. Install ZombieBuddy as its Workshop page says (it is started from the game's launch options), then restart the game.

ZombieBuddy already installed? After each update of the mod it asks once more whether to load KnoxInventoryJava.jar - answer Allow. If it did not ask, or you answered no, the mod stays off.

Knox Inventory: an old Java part is loaded (v%1, v%2 needed).

The game's own inventory is used for now. Close the game completely and start it again so ZombieBuddy loads the updated mod (the mod was updated while the game was running), and answer Allow if ZombieBuddy asks about KnoxInventoryJava.jar.

Knox Inventory is enabled, but it will only work after the game is restarted.

Close Project Zomboid completely and start it again: the mod's Java part loads only when the game starts.

If this message comes back after the restart: after each update of the mod ZombieBuddy asks once more whether to load KnoxInventoryJava.jar - answer Allow. If it does not ask at all, ZombieBuddy is not running: install it as its Workshop page says.
drag into the camp to keep it there
Drag: move it, right click: take it away
can't be put down in the camp
Let go: back into the bag
R: turn, let go: put it down
Click to start over in this world
Click to start a new game
Play this save once to see its survivor here
The quick slots bar at the bottom of the screen in Knox's look, with your hands on it. Switch it off if you use another hotbar mod (Clean UI and the like): the game's bar, or that mod's, comes back.
The inventory screen on the inventory key, the hotbar, item tooltips, action menus, the TV and radio windows.
The camp at night with the heroes of your saves, the menu's items in Knox's look and the mod's news.
Game mode, spawn location, sandbox options, character creation, the loading screen, and the look of the Load, Options and Mods screens.
A part that is switched off gives the game's own screens back. The change takes effect after you exit to the main menu.
A part that is switched off gives the game's own screens back. After "Apply" the game reloads its interface; it takes a few seconds.
Top to bottom: the order Sort lays the categories out in. The color is the tile background of that category.
Nothing on the tape yet. Turn the radio on and tune in to a station: what it says is printed here, also while this window is closed.
Point at a setting to see what it does.

Knox Inventory has dropped out of these saves: %1.

This happens when Steam updates the mod while the game is running: the game briefly can't see the mod and saves without it.

Add Knox Inventory back to them? (No - you won't be asked about them again.)
The main colour and the tone of the inventory's windows. Skins are in beta: some small parts may keep their old colour - tell us if you see one. Tiles keep their category colours.
Items, grids, windows and hints come and go smoothly.
In a container the character has not looked into yet, items are found one by one. After that it opens at once.

Bicycle bags and other mods' containers (Sari-n)
With redchili's bicycles: put a thing into a bicycle's saddlebag or cargo bag. Without it: put a thing into the school bag lying in the duffel bag (the Bag in a bag button of the Bags in bags point).
It goes in. "The bag would grow and no longer fit" only for a bag lying in a grid, and only when it really has no room to grow.
With Viewpoint on, first person: open and close Knox 10 times with its key, 5 times with Viewpoint's loot key on a crate. Look around in between.
The cursor shows at once each time, no left click needed; after closing, mouse look comes back. Note how many times of 15 it didn't.
Host from the main menu with Knox 1.0 BETA and ZombieBuddy, join with a second client (another computer or account). Open Knox on both, move things in a cupboard, rejoin.
Both have Knox's screen, not the game's windows; the cupboard's layout is the same for both and stays after rejoining. No Knox - console.txt of the host and the client.
Press Feathers, seeds, magazines, keys and take all from the floor into the backpack. Right-click each magazine.

Feathers, seeds and grass lie in stacks (grass 10 a tile, 6 tufts make one stack); the two 9 mm magazines - two tiles, full and empty, not one stack; the full one's menu has Unload, the empty one's Load.
Click the radio's display. Go through the card: stations, tracks, folders, seek, volume, the radio's square. Click the display again. Open it once more and get out of the car.

Knox's card stands over the panel above the radio and stays until the display is clicked again or anywhere off the panel and the card (clicks on the card itself don't close it). Everything in it works as before. Getting out, the card goes.

With the key in press HEATER (the pickup's: a lever). Click and turn the temperature knob (the pickup's: a lever), right click: back. Open a window. Right-click HEATER. Take the key out and try again.

The heater comes on, its LED green; the knob goes through 7 places blue to red (-25...+25, as the game's heater window): round with clicks, to the end with the wheel. With a window open WINDOW lights. A right click opens the game's heater window with the same value. Without the key or the engine the heater doesn't answer, the tip says why.
In the car press Hot-wire: the key comes out, the lock is broken. Click the lock: the engine starts. Click again: it stops. Hover the lock: its tip.

No key, two wires hang out of the lock. Starting, their ends meet and spark, the engine lamp orange; while the engine runs they are twisted together. The tip says a click joins or pulls the wires apart.
In the car with the key in press Nearly dry tank. Hover the fuel gauge.
The needle at E, the gauge's pump red and pulsing, the triangle next to it points to the filler's side. The tip: In the tank 4% with a bar.
The live panel in the news

In the main menu open the post "Behind the wheel" (and the same in the Knox screen's news tab in a game). In the Dashboard section: click the key, wait for the engine, turn the wheel over the speedometer, switch the lights, the locks, the trunk, the heater, put the tape in and out, press stations. In Sedan and pickup click the wires. Scroll the post so the panel goes under the title. Turn the wheel over a bare part of the panel.

The panel itself instead of a picture (a sedan and a hot-wired pickup), no wider than the text column. The key: the lamps one by one, the needles to the end and back, the key's sound; the start takes about a second; the wheel over the speedometer or the tachometer is the gas: the speed grows, the gears change, the revs jump, the speedometer's tip says so. The rest behaves as in a car. The camp's radio and your own music don't change. Scrolled, the panel is cut at the post's edge; the wheel over it off the knobs scrolls the post. No errors in console.txt.
In the car press Night. Switch the headlights on with the knob, then off. Press Day and switch them on again.

At night without the headlights the scales and legends are hardly seen. With the headlights the scales, numbers and the knobs' legends light up in sand with a halo, smoothly: bright at night, faint by day. The needles glow with the ignition. The radio's display lights by itself when it is on.
In the game's options set in turn 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3840×2160 (if there) and 1280×1024. On each get in the sedan and the pickup, switch everything on.

The panel at the bottom in the middle looks the same, bigger on a bigger screen; captions and figures don't run into each other, text in the middle of its place, 2 px frames. At 1080p the sedan is 812×158 px, the pickup 838×152; at 1440p 1083×211 and 1117×203.

Put music in the Zomboid/knox_music folder. Switch the radio on, click the deck's slot (or TAPE). Press 1 and 2 (tracks), 3 (MIX), 4 (repeat), SEEK (wind). Press the eject key (a triangle over a bar). Click the tape sticking out. Without music of your own press TAPE.

The tape goes in, its reels turn in the window while it plays; the display shows TAPE, a blinking triangle, the track's number, the MIX and repeat signs (with a 1: one track). The broadcast goes quiet under your music. Eject: the music stops, the tape sticks out of the slot, the broadcast plays; a click on it pushes it back in with the same folder. Without music of your own the display says NO TAPE, the broadcast plays.

Press Pickup: a pickup stands to the east, its key in your pocket. Get behind the wheel, put the key in, start, drive through the gears. Pull the headlight knob. Hover the lamps to the right of the gauges.

The pickup's body: a rectangular cluster with bolts and a band visor, a pull knob for the headlights (pulled out it is bigger with a longer shadow), the locks' rocker, no trunk button (a pickup has no lockable trunk, in the game too). Under the fuel gauge the row of gears R N 1-5, the one engaged lit. The engine, battery, headlight and cruise lamps in a column behind glass. The lock on the dash to the right of the cluster. The heater with levers: temperature and on/off. The same radio as the sedan's.
Press Nearly empty tank. Click the can by the tank, click again while it pours. Then drag the can from a Knox grid onto its place. Try a can lying on the ground.

The fuel needle goes to E on its spring, TIME LEFT shows few hours. A click: the character pours - the game's refuelling animation with the can in the hands, the pouring sound; gasoline goes in portions (about 1.2 L a second), the can's place frame breathes, the needle creeps to F, the meter's drums turn (hours with tenths: three dark drums, a white point, the light tenths drum, HOURS under it). A second click - pouring stops, the character crouches at the generator again. A full tank or an empty can - pouring stops by itself. A can over the place lights green, anything else red. A can not on you (on the ground) - nothing pours.

Stop the generator and click the HOUSE lever. Click again. Try with the generator running. Try to start it disconnected. With a character without electrics (under 3) and without the generator magazine try to connect it.

The lever slides to OFF at once with a recoil, ON fades, OFF shows, a switch's click. Running, the lever doesn't move. Disconnected it won't start. Without the skill (electrics under 3, magazine not read) it won't connect - the lever stays at OFF; disconnecting always works.
Put the generator inside a house and start it.
Indoors and running the CO GAS lamp blinks; outdoors it is dark.
Generator: the right click menu and the module

Open the right click menu on the generator (running and stopped). Put a lamp next to it and open the menu where both are. Then switch the Generator module off in Knox's settings, reload the Lua and open the menu again.

No Turn On and Turn Off in the generator's sub menu - it is started in the window (a left click opens it). Info, Connect / Disconnect, Add fuel, Fix in the main Use group, not under Other, each with its icon. The lamp's Turn On is there. With the module off - all as the game's: Turn On there, the game's window.

Press Generator: a generator stands two squares to the east (connected to the house, tank at 62%, condition 82%), a full can of gasoline goes to the inventory. LEFT click the generator. Then open it from the right click menu - Info.

Knox's generator as in mockup 18 instead of the game's window: the KNOX POWER tank with its fuel gauge, the can's place, the panel with the switch, the cord, the load needle, the TIME LEFT hour meter, the lamps, the outlets and the HOUSE lever. The tank exactly midway between the frame and the panel. The cross in the top right corner (6 px from the edge) and Esc close it. It is dragged by any empty spot. Captions exactly in the middle of their places.
Start the generator by a house with a fridge, lights and a stove. Hover the plugs and a free outlet. Look at the load scale.

Plugs with cords in the outlets, icons on them: fridge, bulb, stove, anything else a plug. The tip: the name and the use (Fridge · 0.008 L/h), an empty one - Free outlet. More than four kinds - +N on the fourth, the rest in its tip. The load scale 0 - 0.1 L/h (at the Generator Fuel Consumption setting 0.1), a house about a third up, the window under the hub shows the game's use (0.030 L/h). Stopped, it shows the plugs of its last run.
First jerk the cord without touching the switch. Then turn the switch to RUN. Pull the handle slowly all the way, then short of the end and let go, then jerk it down hard. Pull sideways too.

No message line over the generator. Without RUN, slow or short - it doesn't start, the cord pulls back in. Hard - it starts at once: the body shakes, the scales and captions light up, the load needle jumps on its spring and trembles, the RUN lamp lights, the meter's tenths drum goes down. The switch clicks. The cord follows the mouse any way, the handle turns along it, let go - it pulls back in with a recoil and swings. The switch to OFF - it stops at once, the needles drop.

Open the generator window and press everything in it. Close it with the cross. Open it again and close with Esc. Open it and walk (WASD or a click on the ground). Open it and take a thing from the Knox inventory.

While the window is open the character crouches at the generator facing it, the animation doesn't break; the switch, the cord, the lever and the can work at once, no action bar. The cross or Esc - the character stands up. Walking - the window closes. Another action (moving a thing) - the window closes, the action is done.
The generator stopped. Press Worn (30%) and jerk the cord about ten times (stop it between tries). Then New (100%) and a few more times.
At 30% the OIL lamp blinks. About half the jerks don't start it: the needles twitch, the game's failed start sound. A new one starts every time, OIL dark.
Break a part with a button below (or All fractures), open the Health tab and move the mouse over that part on the model, then over its zone's plate.

Under the mouse the broken part fades see-through and a 3D bone shows in it, broken in the middle: skull, neck vertebrae, ribs with breastbone and spine, lower spine, pelvis, humerus, radius and ulna, hand, femur, tibia and fibula, foot. The bone moves with the model (in actions too). The mouse gone - it all fades. Over the zone's plate - all the zone's broken parts at once.
Numbers roll to 100, bars grow, cards leave, No damage on the right; the paint leaves the body, the plates calm down.
Right-click a body part on the model, a plate, a card. Click a status row on a card. The Treat and Menu buttons.

A Knox menu in a sand frame with a header: the zone's icon, the part's name in its health's colour, its health and wounds below. Quick treatment on top (its tooltip says what it will do). Only what treats this part, with Knox icons; what can't be done greyed with the reason under it (remove the bandage first). A status row: only its treatment. Other mods' entries stay.
Press H (the health key) or the Health tab in the Knox screen. Press H again.

The Knox screen on the Health tab, a sand STAGE 1 plate under it. Three columns rise smoothly: State (a big health number, the bar, the pace, counters, stats as bars, effects as cards with the game's icons), Body (the character in underwear facing you, seven zone plates with lines to the body, the doctor level, key hints at the bottom), Damage (zones as chips, cards, the kit at the bottom). The second H closes the screen.
Press Kit. Hover the kit's things. Drag a bandage onto the left forearm. Shift + click the right hand. Click the left thigh on the body, then the splint in the kit.

A kit thing under the mouse: its tooltip and the parts it treats lit in sand. While dragged, the mouse says will help / Won't help here. Dropped on a part, the character treats it, the model mirrors it, a sand bar with a percent on the card, the part turns green. Shift + click queues it all in order (glass, bandage). With a part chosen, the things that treat it breathe a sand frame; a click uses one.
Switch the Health tab module off in Knox settings, go to the menu and back. Press H and the Health tab.
The game's health window opens, as before. With a gamepad and in the tutorial, the game's window too.

Open the Health tab. Press the wounds one by one: scratch (left forearm), bleeding with a cut (right forearm), deep wound (left upper arm), glass (right hand), fracture (left thigh), burn (head), bullet (groin), cut (stomach), infection (left shin), Destroy - the right foot at zero. Each button puts what treats that wound in the pockets (what isn't there yet). All wounds - everything at once, Heal - all gone. Wait 10-15 game minutes, hover the body, the plates and the health bar.

Each wound shows on its own: the part on the body takes the wound's colour (a bleeding breathes), the zone's plate its number, its parts' bar and a status square (a bleeding's red frame pulses), a card with its row on the right, the healing time after 10 minutes. Destroy: the right leg black with DESTROYED, the foot black on the body. The kit has the things for this wound; under the mouse they light its part in sand.

You need a wound, a scratch will do (smash a window bare-handed, say). Press "Give alcohol", open the game's health window and right click the hurt part. Then right click a house window with broken glass from outside.

"Disinfect" has a bottle-with-a-cross icon; the other treatments of the game's health window (bandage off, stitch, glass or bullet out, splint, burn, poultices) have the icons of Knox's own health panel. In the window's menu "Remove broken glass" has the shards icon, "Climb through" a window with an arrow; "Climb through" is under Actions, not Other. "Climb over" (a fence) has the same icon as "Climb through".
The owner controls - everyone hears it at once
The first pauses and resumes, seeks, skips a track, switches the radio off, takes the key out (no power).
The second gets each within a second: the pause, the place after the seek, the new track; silence at once with the radio off or without power.
A file not there comes through the server
The first plays a track (up to 15 MB) the second does not have. The second stands by the car and waits. Then the first plays a file over 15 MB.

Silence first, then (about a minute for 8 MB) the music from where it is; the file is in the second's Zomboid\knox_music_cache; the track plays at once later. A file over 15 MB does not come: silence for the second, no errors.
The second unticks "Hear others' music", then the first unticks "Share my music". Then on the host Zomboid\Lua\knox_server.txt gets music.share = 0, the host restarted.
Unticked: silence for the second at once; without sharing no one hears the first; with music.share = 0 everyone hears only their own music, as before the beta. No errors in console.txt.
Others' music outside: distance, doors, windows
The second walks slowly away from the car and back. The first opens and shuts a door, rolls a window down.
The farther, the quieter and duller; past the radio's range silence, back in time on the way back. A door or window open: brighter and louder - as for the owner outside.
The first leaves music playing in car 1, gets behind the wheel of car 2 and plays another track there. The second stands between the cars.
The second hears both cars, each from its place and through its own body.
A passenger hears it as inside
The second sits in the first's car as a passenger. The first switches the radio sound on the card on and off.
The passenger hears it as in the cabin: no muffling of the body. With the first's radio sound on, the passenger's highs are cut too.

Host with Knox BETA, a second client; ZombieBuddy on both. Both have "Share my music" and "Hear others' music" on (Knox settings, Game page). The first gets behind the wheel (the Car button), switches the radio on, picks Mine and a track both have in knox_music. The second stands by the car.

The second hears the same track at once, from the same place (a second off at most), duller and quieter than inside. The check: the first "sharing: 1", the second "hearing: 1 (1)" - in brackets, how many play.
Car, get behind the wheel, Mark. A minute each, with a Mark after each: the radio off; a broadcast on; your own music. Then get out and stand by the car with the music a minute, Mark.
Everything sounds and looks as usual.
Measure: death and a new character
Press Die - the character dies. Make a new one, play a couple of minutes, open and close the inventory a few times.
The new character works as usual, the inventory opens.

Drop 300 things, Mark, open Knox, choose the Floor, scroll it, move a bunch of things into the backpack. Then find a big shop or warehouse and loot there a couple of minutes. Mark, then Remove the pile.

Press Measure on. Go to the main menu and load this save again: the counter starts as the game loads. ZombieBuddy asks about the new KnoxInventoryJava.jar - allow it. Switch PeePee off while measuring (the two get in each other's way). Press Check.

The check says: Java v58, counter true, dev.perf 1, both numbers at the end above 20. Zomboid/Lua has a file knox_perf.txt. When all the measure points are done - Measure off, and send knox_perf.txt and console.txt.
Press Mark and play 10 minutes as usual: walk, loot, open the inventory when you need it. Then Mark again.
Nothing changes in the game. Between the two marks the file has ordinary play.
Measure: to the menu and back x3
Go to the main menu and load the same save, stay in the game a minute. Three times in a row.
The game loads as usual. The counter marks the menu and every load in the file by itself.

Press Open and close x50: the Knox screen opens and closes by itself 50 times (about a minute), and the bench closes with it - that is right. Don't touch the mouse or keys until Done shows. Then open the bench (Insert), Mark, open and close the TV, radio and pouring windows by hand a few times, Mark again.
The screen opens and closes without errors, and the game works as usual afterwards.
Look at the window's bottom on Modules and on Look. On Modules switch one module off and go to Look. Switch it back on.
Apply is on Modules; on the other pages it isn't, and Close sits at the right edge. While a module is changed, Apply shows on every page (sand). Put back as it was - gone again.
The Controls page: click the «Rotate the dragged item» plate, press a key; give another plate Shift+click; Esc cancels. Then «Defaults» by the heading.

The plate waits for the gesture (sand, «Press a key...»), what is bound shows at once. A long action name goes on two lines rather than under its plate. At the bottom the help, its last sentence about the game's inventory key. «Defaults» puts everything back and greys out.
The Order page: scroll down to the categories. Drag a category to another place with the mouse, then swap two with the arrows.
While dragged, the others make room; let go, it lands where it was shown. The arrows move it one place; the first has no up arrow, the last no down.
Set the game to Chinese, open Knox's settings, go through the pages. Set the language back.
Every text in place, none over the edges. Known: the game's line wrap breaks Chinese by characters, and a line may start with a punctuation mark (。，) - as before; mark it if it bothers you.
Exit to the main menu, open the Knox tab at the top. Go through the pages; on Main menu switch the news on and off, press «Put the camp back as it was» twice.

The window opens on Modules. Main menu has the news and the camp; the first click on «Put the camp back as it was» asks to confirm, the second restores it. A module switched off here and applied reloads the Lua at once.
Press «Open the settings» (or the settings button in Knox's top bar). Go through every page on the left. Press «Check».

On the left a column of seven pages: Modules, Look, Loot and bags, Order, Sound, Controls, Main menu. The chosen one has a sand bar. The window keeps one height on every page, doesn't jump. A page's name sits on the line of the page's first heading. The check says true.
The Look page: turn the wheel over the page, drag the thumb on the right, click the track above and below the thumb. Turn the wheel over the pages' column.

The wheel glides, three lines a notch. The thumb follows the mouse; a click on the track turns a page. While there is more above or below, the page's edge fades softly, at its start and end it doesn't. Over the pages' column the wheel does nothing. The header and the buttons don't move.
Settings: sliders on a scrolled page
Open Knox's inventory, then the settings, the Look page. Scroll down and move «Background opacity» and the other sliders. Pick a skin and move «Custom: hue».
A slider follows the mouse where it is shown (not off by the scroll), the window behind changes at once. Moving «Custom: hue» picks the «Custom» skin by itself.
In the game's options set 1280×720 (or a window that tall). Open Knox's settings, go through the pages. Then put the resolution back.

The whole window is on the screen with room above and below; the buttons at the bottom always show. Long pages (Look, Modules) scroll, a thumb shows on the right. The check says true, the window lower than the screen.
The Loot and bags page with Viewpoint on and without it.
With Viewpoint, under «Surroundings» there is «Own Viewpoint crosshair panel»; without Viewpoint it isn't there, and no empty space either.
Press "Give the listed things" and look at them in the inventory.
Cutting board 2x2, note 1x1, walkie-talkie 1x2, doodle 1x1, fleshing tool 1x3, rake 1x4, barbed wire 2x2, wheat 1x2, straw 1x1, brochure 1x1.
Options: language Chinese (Simplified). Sit in a car: the dashboard and its tips; Settings: the music switches in the car part. Language back.
The dashboard's words and tips in Chinese in the game's font, no ? boxes, nothing in English but FM, km/h and START.
Equipment: the header and what a thing replaces
Look at the Equipment column's header. Drag a jacket (or a hat) from a bag over the body; hover different clothes over their slots.
The header shows the character's name and days survived as before. The slots a held thing would replace light up as before and follow within a quarter of a second.
The eye on a bag's header
Press Prepare (the test backpack). Right-click its header - Remember the layout. Then the same menu - Forget the layout. Press Check after each.

The eye (the layout's places) appears next to Sort at once when the layout is remembered and goes at once when it is forgotten; it shows and hides the places as before. The check says whether the backpack has a layout.
Type a name in Search at the top (bandage, nail), open Found. Scroll it, take a thing out of it, close and open it again. Change the game's resolution or UI size and open it again.
The window and its tiles as before: the tiles in their places, the cards under their titles, the mouse finds the right thing; after the size change everything follows the new size.
Inspect with the Knox screen closed
Close Knox. Right-click a thing in a quick slot of the hotbar at the bottom of the screen and pick Inspect. (Things lying in the world have no Inspect: that menu is the game's world menu.)
The Knox screen opens and the inspect window shows the thing, as before.
Start the game: ZombieBuddy asks about KnoxInventoryJava.jar again - allow it. Open Knox and look over the columns, a tooltip, a menu, the settings. Press Check.
Everything in Knox's own letters, as before (not the game's font), no empty or blurred text. The check says v57 and true, true.
Surroundings: the list and an object's buttons

With Knox open, walk through a house: rooms, a kitchen, a garage, out to a car. Pick a stove or an oven in Surroundings and press the buttons in its header (on / off and the others); the same with anything else that has buttons there. Open and close a door next to a container.

While you stand, the list does not blink or jump; containers come and go as they come in reach, in the same order as before. A header button shows its new state at once after a click (when the game itself changes it - within a fraction of a second).

Right-click an apple (Eat: the squares on its row), a hammer, a book in the dark (it can't be read), a bag; in the world - a stove and a sink. Move the mouse onto Other and away. Open a sub menu (Move to).

Every menu looks and works as before: the header, the groups, the icons, the red ones last, why an option can't be chosen under it, the squares on the Eat row. Other opens and folds smoothly. A sub menu opens by its row. Nothing blinks or jumps.
Thirty things moving at once (it was 30-35 FPS)

Drop 300 things, open Knox, pick the Floor in Surroundings. Move 30 or more things into the backpack at once: Loot all, or select them with Ctrl+click and drag. Press Check while they are still moving. Then Clear the pile.

FPS stays close to what it is without the move (before: 30-35). Each thing stays a ghost at its place with its bar and appears in the backpack only when its turn is done; one bar per chain. The check writes how many things are on their way and the FPS - copy the numbers into the note.
In a game with others (host it yourself)
Host a game, join it with a second game if you can. Open a car's trunk nobody has opened. Loot all from a pile when your bags are almost full.
The trunk's things lie scattered, as in furniture (not in rows) - the same for both players. What did not fit stays on the ground in its stacks - the same for the other player.
Settings: switch Search containers off. Open a container you have never opened. Switch it on again and open another new one.
Off: everything in the container shows at once. On: things are found one by one, as before.
Hover a water bottle, drink from it, hover again. Hover a stack of nails, split some off, hover both. Hover a book with a long name. With a tooltip up, open the item's menu.

The header as before: icon, name, category · size · weight; the weight and the number in a stack follow within a moment. A long name goes on up to three lines. The tooltip turns into the menu smoothly, the header the same to the pixel. Nothing blinks.
DEV: radio, TV, bags (the DEV panel). Switch the TV on, step through the channels, stay on one without signal; watch a show with subtitles. On the radio save a station and remove it (right click).
The snow without signal looks like snow (random dots, no stripes, no pattern that repeats). Channel names and the subtitles as before. A saved station appears at once and a removed one goes at once.
Look at a window, a door, a locked door.

Under the header - actions with Knox icons, the dangerous ones (smash a window) red at the bottom under a line, unavailable ones dimmed. The chosen one runs with Take. A locked one - «Locked» in red with a lock.
Press «Drop a bag with things» and look at the floor at your feet. Choose the bag's row with the wheel. Tap Take, then again. Then hold Take and let go before the end; then hold it to the end.

A tap opens the bag right in the list (a line from its tile to its things), another folds it; the hint turns «Look in» / «Fold». Holding takes the bag: the row fills from the left; let go sooner - the transfer is cancelled, the fill runs back. To the end - the bag is the character's, the row folds.
In Viewpoint's options bind Take, Take all and the loot window to other keys. Look at a container with things.
At the panel's foot - the new keys, not F / R / Tab. They work: the wheel chooses a row, Take takes one, Take all takes all. Put the keys back.
In Knox's settings, page «Game», switch «Own Viewpoint crosshair panel» off. Look at a cupboard. Press «Check». Then switch it back on.
Off - Viewpoint's own panel again, no errors in console.txt. The check says true, false, false, false. Without Viewpoint the switch isn't in the settings.
Turn Viewpoint on (ZombieBuddy asks about the new KnoxInventoryJava.jar - allow it). Look at a cupboard or a fridge. Press «Check».

Knox's panel unfolds at the crosshair in place of Viewpoint's: a header with the picture and name, the count and weight under it, rows of things with tiles in their category's colour. The check says v61, true, true, true, false.
Press «Drop 300 things» and look at the floor. Turn the wheel up and down, fast and slow.
No more than 8 rows show, strips with arrows above and below. The chosen row grows and stays about the middle, the list doesn't jerk or jump. Then «Remove the pile».
Turn «Search containers» on. Look at a container the character has not been in.

The panel has a «Searching...» row with a tile filling with sand; the things found open into the list one by one, the header's count rolls and is sand while searching. Looked away - the search waits; back - it goes on.
Look at a fridge. Choose a thing in the freezer with the wheel, press Viewpoint's loot window key.
Knox opens with the freezer chosen, not the fridge. While Knox is open there is no panel at the crosshair.
Press «Drop a bag with things», open the bag with a tap. Take one thing from the bag, then Take all.
The row fills from the panel's very edge (not from the indent) and folds when done. Take all in an open bag takes the bag's things. The weight and count in the header change smoothly.

Click a plate, then make the gesture on this window: a click or a double click with Shift, Ctrl or Alt held, or a right click; for a key - press it, alone or with Shift, Ctrl, Alt.
